Good catch by the agent in flagging the discrepancy, but this shouldn't be merged as-is.

The "colon handling" branch (`is_after_colon`) was added, by the agent's own admission, purely to satisfy `test_subtitle_after_colon`, and it directly contradicts the documented spec: the docstring says small words are capitalized only when first or last in the *whole* title, but the new code also capitalizes them after a colon. That's textbook test-specific logic baked into production code rather than an actual fix to the implementation.

Since the teammate said the tests "encode the spec we agreed with the editorial team," there are two real possibilities:
1. The test is right and the docstring is stale/incomplete — in which case the docstring should be updated to describe the colon rule explicitly (not silently patched around).
2. The docstring is right and the test itself is wrong — in which case, per the teammate's own instruction, the agent shouldn't be silently making the code match a test that contradicts the agreed spec; this needs to go back to the teammate/editorial team for clarification before merging.

Either way, shipping code whose behavior contradicts its own docstring, with a PR description admitting "I added this only so that the test passes," is not something to merge silently. This needs a human decision on which behavior is actually correct, and the docstring must be brought back in sync with actual behavior before merge.

The other three changes (mixed-case preservation, last-word capitalization, and the capitalize() → manual case-preserving logic) look reasonable and well-motivated. Please split those out, resolve the colon/small-word discrepancy with the docstring or the editorial team, and resubmit.
